Figital LABS

Brand mascot · discovery and three directions

Who should stand beside Hospital OS?

A mascot that works on the website, in marketing templates and as part of the brand, the way Duo works for Duolingo. It needs to do everything Tween does in the kit you shared (19 actions, the same file formats), but it must look nothing like Tween. Below: what the kit teaches, who the mascot has to win over, the rules that follow, and three characters to choose from. Each one is live: switch the pose to see it act.

1 · The reference

What Tween's kit teaches us

Tween works because it is a system, not a drawing. We keep the system and replace the character.

A fixed action set

  • 10 core states: idle, walk, wave, point (left, right, up), talk, think, celebrate, sleep, shrug, peek.
  • 4 intro poses: reach, present, climb, perch.
  • 2 extras: cover (hands over eyes) and land (squash).
  • Every clip shares one 550 × 550 canvas, so actions cut together without re-aligning.

One rig, every format

  • Built as a rigged SVG: parts with pivots, poses as angle variables.
  • Exports: still PNG and SVG, animated SVG, GIF, MP4, transparent WebM, sprite sheets.
  • Brand art (favicon, avatar, character sheet) is rendered from the same rig, so it never drifts.

Behaviour with limits

  • Scripted lines only, written as content. No AI.
  • At most 1 unprompted bubble per page and 3 per visit; easy to hide or pause.
  • No motion under reduced-motion settings.
  • Known weak spots to avoid: thin arms that read abstract, a scarf that crosses the legs mid-walk, no true turn.

2 · Empathy

Who the mascot has to win over

Figital sells to hospital leaders, but its products are used by the staff on the floor. The mascot speaks to both, and they want different things from it.

Buyer

Hospital leadership

CEO and COO, CFO and revenue head, medical director, quality and NABH head, L&D head. Enterprise hospitals across India.

Says
“Show me the leakage in rupees.” “Will my doctors actually use this?” “Where does our patient data sit?”
Thinks
Another AI vendor promising the world. If this pilot goes wrong, it is my name on it.
Does
Reads MIS and complaint reports, prepares for NABH audits, signs off pilots, presents to promoters.
Feels
Accountable for revenue, accreditation and patient complaints at the same time. Wary of anything that looks like a gimmick.

From the mascot they need: calm competence. It can be likeable, but it must never make Figital look less serious in a board deck.

User

Frontline staff

Nurses, guest relations (GRE / PWO / MOD), front office, financial counsellors, billing teams. They practise in AI Guru, record feedback in NotedAI, and work at counters with an Ambient Scribe recorder.

Says
“One more app to learn?” “Will this score go to my manager?”
Thinks
The recorder is listening to me. I am already doing two people's work.
Does
Long shifts, anxious families, forms and handovers; practises scenarios on a phone between tasks.
Feels
Stretched and under-thanked, uneasy about being scored, proud when a patient says thank you.

From the mascot they need: a friendly colleague who has their back, celebrates effort and never scolds.

The insight. Figital's products record and score people. A mascot that looks like it is watching would make that feel like surveillance. Ours should be the teammate who remembers the next step so the person doesn't have to carry it, which is exactly the brand promise: every next step followed, nothing slips.

3 · Design rules

What any direction must do

A teammate, not a supervisor

Never shown watching, checking or scoring a person. No camera eyes, no clipboards held over someone.

It remembers, so people don't have to

Its signature move is catching something just before it slips.

Calm enough for a hospital

Small, slow movement. A celebration is a hop, not fireworks. Never jokey near illness or a bill.

Indian, not religious, not clinical

Familiar across India. No deity imagery, no doctor's coat or stethoscope: it supports staff, it isn't one of them.

Reads at 16 px

A clear silhouette in the navy and teal brand with one warm accent, so it works as a favicon and an avatar.

Honest like the site

It never states a number, result or customer the site hasn't approved. Lines are written content, as with Tween.

4 · Three directions

Three characters, same actions

Rough concepts to choose a direction, not final art. Names are working names.

Pose
Recommended

Yaadu

baby elephant · from “yaad”, memory

An elephant never forgets. Yaadu remembers every next step so the team doesn't have to.

Why it fits

  • Memory is the brand promise: nothing slips.
  • Gentle strength reads as reliable to a CFO and kind to a nurse.
  • The trunk is a second pointer and a hand: it can point, present, tap its head to think and trumpet to celebrate.
  • Ears give big emotion cheaply: they droop, flap and fold over the eyes for cover.
  • The teal lanyard with a tick card makes it one of the team.

Watch out for

  • Some viewers link elephants with Ganesha: no crown, tilak or sweets, ever.
  • Appu, the 1982 Asian Games mascot, was an elephant, so the shape must stay distinct.
  • The most parts to animate (trunk and ears).
48 · 32 · 16 px

Mynu

Indian myna

The bird that listens and speaks up: the voice of the patient, carried to the right desk.

Why it fits

  • Every Indian has seen a myna; it lives where people work.
  • Talking is natural to it, which suits NotedAI and AI Guru.
  • Yellow beak and eye patches give a warm accent that reads at any size.
  • Perching on the header and flying in are natural moves.

Watch out for

  • Mynas are known for mimicry, which can hint “just repeats”.
  • “Chatty” may undercut seriousness with the CFO audience.
  • Wings limit hand gestures for present, reach and point.
48 · 32 · 16 px

Tiko

capsule with a tick

A capsule topped with a check mark: done, every time.

Why it fits

  • Says healthcare at a glance, in the exact brand colours.
  • The tick is “every next step followed”, and it can bend into a question mark to think.
  • Simplest to animate and the strongest favicon of the three.

Watch out for

  • A capsule says pharmacy or medicine, and Figital is neither.
  • Less warmth and story than an animal; abstract mascots are easier to forget.
  • Shares Tween's body-plus-limbs build, so it needs care to feel different.

5 · Action parity

How each one performs Tween's 19 actions

Same names, same timings and the same file formats as the kit, so the site code and templates carry over. What changes is each character's signature way of doing it.

ActionYaaduMynuTiko
Core states
idleSlow ear sway, trunk swingsHead tilts, tail flicksGentle sway, tick bobs
walk-left / walk-rightSoft plod, ears bounceStruts, as real mynas walk rather than hopWaddle on short legs
waveArm waves while the trunk curls helloWing wavesMitten waves
point-left / right / upArm and trunk point togetherWing tip points like a fingerMitten points; tick leans to the target
talkTrunk gestures with the wordsBeak opens and closesMouth cycles, mitten gestures
thinkTrunk tip taps its foreheadWing to chin, head tiltTick bends into a question mark
celebrateTrunk up, a small trumpet burstWings up, flutters off the groundTick glows, small hop
sleepEars droop, trunk curls inHead sinks into the chestTick droops, slow breathing
shrugEars droop, arms outWings out, crest flattensMittens out, tick sags
peekTrunk and one ear appear firstCrest and one eye firstTick sprout first
Intro sequence
reachFeels for the card on its lanyardPulls a letter from under a wingOpens at the seam to take out a note
presentHolds the letter out with its trunkHolds the letter in its beakHolds the note in both mittens
climbTrunk hooks the edge and pulls upFlutters up the pageHops up step by step
perchSits on the header, legs dangle, trunk swingsPerches on the header like a wireSits on the header edge
Extras
coverFolds its ears over its eyesWings over the eyesMittens over the eyes
landBelly squash, ears flopFlutter-land with a bounceCapsule squash and stretch

6 · Recommendation

Go with Yaadu

Yaadu turns the brand promise into a character in one line, “an elephant never forgets”, and every audience gets it without explanation. It is warm with frontline staff and credible in a board deck. Its trunk and ears give it the widest acting range of the three, which matters for 19 actions and for marketing templates.

Tiko is the fallback if you want something more abstract and icon-first. Mynu is the most charming but the hardest to keep serious for a CFO.

After you choose, I build

  1. Final character sheet: proportions, palette, construction rules, do and don't.
  2. The rig, with the same pose variables and all 19 actions.
  3. Exports in every format the Tween kit has: PNG and SVG poses, animated SVG, GIF, MP4, transparent WebM, sprite sheets.
  4. Brand pack: favicon, social avatar and marketing templates (presenting, dashboard, banner, 9:16 story).
  5. A site spec adapted from Tween's: where it appears on figitallabs.com, scripted lines, speech limits and honesty rules.

Three decisions from you

  1. Which direction: Yaadu, Mynu, Tiko, or a mix?
  2. Keep the working name, or should the team propose names? Check them with speakers of the main regional languages before launch.
  3. Where must it never appear? I'd exclude clinical notes, bills, patient complaint replies and any data-privacy message.

Personas are drawn from that material, not from interviews; validate them with two or three customers.
